newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Health Min details CPMF check tax spending.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Health Min details CPMF check tax spending.

text.p: The Brazilian Health Ministry said it aimed to raise 5.31 billion reais from a new financial transaction tax over the next 13 months.
The so-called CPMF "check tax" comes into force Thursday and levies 0.2 percent on all financial transactions.
The ministry, in a statement, gave the following breakdown for its planned spending of the revenue from the CPMF tax:
-- 1.16 billion reais would be transferred to hospitals to cover payments to suppliers for deliveries dating back to 1996.
-- 1.74 billion reais would be passed to hospitals belonging to the national health system to cover costs in 1997.
-- 478 million reais will be spent on community disease prevention programmes and family health.
-- 90 million reais will go towards a government-sponsored milk distribution programme for children.
-- 240 million reais will be spent on dengue fever and yellow fever eradication programmes and 150 million reais will be used to combat malaria and other insect-born diseases.
-- 150 million reais will go towards buying medicine.
-- 1.302 billion reais will be used to make up overdue ministry contributions to an employee social security fund.
